translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets: “See, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, and he will prepare your way.”
“The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism for the forgiveness of sins.
The whole region of Judea and the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were all baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
John wore camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
He proclaimed, “One stronger than I is coming. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals.
I indeed baptized with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
Jesus went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
Simon and those who were with him went after him.
When they found him, they said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
He said to them, “Let us go to the nearby villages and towns, so that I may preach there too, for that is why I came.”
He preached in their synagogues throughout Galilee and drove out demons.
A man with leprosy came to him, pleading with him, falling to his knees, and saying to him, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Moved with compassion, Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him, “I am willing. Be clean.”
When he said this, the leprosy immediately left the man, and he became clean.
After sternly warning him, he immediately sent him away.
He said to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone. Instead, go and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
Jesus entered Capernaum, and word spread that he was in the house.
Immediately, so many people gathered that there was no longer room, not even at the door. And he spoke the word to them.
They came to him bringing a paralyzed man, carried by four men.
Since they could not get near him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof above where he was. After digging through it, they lowered the bed on which the paralyzed man lay.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Some of the scribes were sitting there, thinking in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak blasphemy like this? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus immediately knew in his spirit that they were thinking this to themselves, and he said to them, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
“Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
“But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man,
“I tell you, get up and pick up your mat.”
And he immediately went out in front of everyone, so that they were all amazed and praised God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
As Jesus passed by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he got up and followed him.
And while he was reclining at the table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many who followed him.
When the scribes and Pharisees saw him eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples, “Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “The healthy do not need a doctor, but the sick do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Jesus was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make their way along, picking heads of grain.
And the Pharisees said to him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?”
And he said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, both he and those who were with him?
“How he entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which only the priests were permitted to eat, and also gave some to those who were with him?”
And he said to them, “The Sabbath was made for humankind, not humankind for the Sabbath.
“Therefore the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
And he entered the synagogue again, and a man with a withered hand was there.
And they watched him closely to see whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
And he said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand here in the middle.”
And he said to them, “Is it permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they remained silent.

And he looked around at them in anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored, as healthy as the other.
A large crowd followed Jesus and pressed around him.
And there was a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered greatly under many doctors and had spent everything she had, but had gained no benefit at all and had instead grown worse.
Having heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his garment.
For she said, “If I touch even his garment, I will be healed.”
And immediately the source of her bleeding dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
And immediately Jesus, sensing within himself that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothes?”
And his disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
And he looked around to see the woman who had done this.
But the woman, afraid and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
King Herod heard the report about Christ, for his name had become known, and he said, “John has risen from the dead, and that is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
Others said, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”
But when Herod heard this, he said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
For Herod himself had sent men to arrest John and had bound him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, whom he had married.
For John had said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
But Herodias was angry with him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him. When he listened to him, he did many things, and he listened to him gladly.
And an opportune day came when Herod held a banquet on his birthday for his officials, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
And when Herodias’s daughter came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those dining with him. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” And she said, “The head of John the Baptist.”
And she hurried in to the king and made her request, saying, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter right now.”
And the king was deeply distressed, but because of his oath and those dining with him, he did not want to refuse her.
And immediately the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring John’s head. He went and beheaded him in prison.
And he brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And when his disciples heard about it, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gathered around Jesus and reported everything to him, all that they had done and all that they had taught.
Jesus left the regions of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, within the region of the Decapolis.
And they brought to him a man who was deaf and unable to speak, and begged him to lay his hand on him.
Taking him aside from the crowd, he put his fingers into his ears, spat, and touched his tongue.
Looking up to heaven, he sighed and said, “Ephphatha,” which means, “Be opened.”
Immediately his ears were opened, the bond on his tongue was loosened, and he spoke clearly.
He ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more he ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
They were utterly amazed and said, “He does everything well. He makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”
Jesus and his disciples went out into the region of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do people say that I am?”
They answered, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and still others one of the prophets.”
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered him, “You are the Christ.”
He ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer greatly, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise again after three days.
“Whoever wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the gospel will save it.
What good is it for someone to gain the whole world and lose his own soul?
For what can someone give in exchange for his soul?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”
He said to them, “Truly I tell you, some of those standing here will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power.”
“Teacher, I brought you my son, who has a spirit that makes him mute.
Whenever it seizes him, he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
He answered, “O unbelieving generation, how long will I be among you? How long must I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
They brought him to him. When the spirit saw him, it immediately threw the boy into convulsions. He fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
He asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He said, “Since childhood.
It has often thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, everything is possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the child’s father cried out with tears, “I believe, Lord! Help my unbelief!”
When Jesus saw that a crowd was rushing together, he rebuked the unclean spirit and said to it, “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter him again.”
And after crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out. And he became like a dead man, so that many said he was dead.
But Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and he stood up.
When he had entered the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not cast it out?”
And he said to them, “This kind cannot come out by any means except prayer and fasting.”
And leaving that place, they went through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.
For he was teaching his disciples and saying to them, “The Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, and they will kill him. And after he has been killed, he will rise on the third day.”
Jesus and his disciples came to Capernaum. And when he was in the house, he asked his disciples, “What were you discussing among yourselves on the road?”
But they kept silent, for on the road they had been arguing with one another about who was greatest.
And he sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the least of all and the servant of all.”
And he took a child and placed the child in their midst. And taking the child in his arms, he said to them,
“Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.”
John answered him, saying, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name who does not follow us, and we forbade him.”
But Jesus said, “Do not forbid him, for no one who performs a miracle in my name can soon afterward speak evil of me.
For whoever is not against you is for you.
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you bear Christ’s name and belong to him—truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.”
Jesus took his twelve disciples aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to him:
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
And they will mock him, flog him, spit on him, and kill him. And on the third day he will rise.”
And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came before him, saying to him, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask you.”
And Jesus said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
And they said to him, “Grant that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.”
But Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
And they said, “We can.” And Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
But to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to grant, but is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
And when the ten heard this, they began to be indignant with James and John.
Jesus called them to him and said to them, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
But it is not so among you. Whoever wants to become greater among you must be the servant of all.
And whoever wants to be first among you must be the slave of all.
For the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
A certain scribe approached Jesus and asked him, “Which commandment is the first of all?”
Jesus answered him, “The first of all the commandments is: ‘Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.’ This is the first of all the commandments.
The second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these two.”
The scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher. You speak the truth: he is one, and there is no other besides him.
And to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is greater than burnt offerings.”
When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question him any further.
Jesus spoke as he taught in the temple, saying, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is David's son?
For he himself said through the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.’
David himself calls him Lord, so how is he his son?” And the large crowd listened to him gladly.
The soldiers seized Jesus and led him into the courtyard to Caiaphas, that is, the praetorium, and they called together the whole cohort.
They dressed him in purple, wove a crown of thorns, and put it on him.
And they began to salute him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They struck him on the head with a reed and spat on him, and bending their knees, they bowed down before him.
When they had mocked him, they stripped the purple robe off him and dressed him in his own clothes. Then they led him out to crucify him.
They pressed into service a certain passerby, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which means “Place of the Skull.”
They offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he did not take it.
They crucified him and divided his clothes, casting lots for them to determine who would take what.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
The inscription stating the charge against him read: “Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
And two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and the other on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled that says, “He was counted among the lawless.”
And those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
save yourself and come down from the cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests, mocking him among themselves with the scribes, said, “He saved others, but can he not save himself?
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe in him.”
Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member, came. He too was [?] the kingdom of God. Taking courage, he went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was surprised that he had already died. He summoned the centurion and asked him whether he had already died.
And after learning this from the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
Joseph bought a linen shroud, took him down, wrapped him in the shroud, and laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph watched where he was laid.
When the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they might go and anoint Jesus.
Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
And they said to one another, “Who will roll the stone away from the entrance of the tomb for us?”
And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.
And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, dressed in a white robe, and they were [?].
And he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look, this is the place where he was laid.
But go and tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.”
And they went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had seized them. And they said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.
After rising early on the first day of the week, Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
She went and told those who had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
But when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe.
After [?], he appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking into the countryside.
And those two went and told the others, but they did not believe them either.
Later he appeared to the eleven as they reclined at a meal, and rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him after he had risen from the dead.
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the gospel to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
they will pick up snakes in their hands; and if they drink anything deadly, it will not harm them at all. They will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
Then the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
And they went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the signs that accompanied it. Amen.
